newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse ends lower after record highs.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse ends lower after record highs.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange on Friday reversed its recent bull run to close lower. Since last Friday the market had set at new record highs each day.
Traders attributed the decline to profit-taking as one major brokerage unloaded some one billion forints worth of shares onto the market.
The BUX index closed at 3,707.45 points, down 21.13. Spot share turnover totalled 1.98 billion forints.
"One brokerage liquidated a portfolio worth at least one billion forints," Attila Gazdik of New York Broker Budapest said.
"The portfolio included mainly MOL and also OTP, TVK, Richter, Egis and Danubius," he added.
The holder of this portfolio was ready to unload the shares at prices well below prevailing SEAQ prices, Gazdik said.

All the papers Gazdik mentioned, closed lower. Oil firm MOL shares fell 75 forint to end at 1,730, hotelier Danubius plummeted 115 forints to end at 3,000 and chemicals firm TVK lost 35 forints to finish at 1,365.
The pharmaceuticals also closed weaker -- Richter at 8,450 forints, down 75, and Egis at 9,850, down 70.
OTP was only a little weaker ending at 2,665, down five.
Chemical maker Borsodchem was among the few to buck the trend, rising to a new high of 3,220 forints before ending at 3,200, up 40.

Gazdik said that based on Friday's prices it was too early to say whether this was only a one-off profit-taking or the start of a declining trend. However he said it was a healthy correction after the market's gains this week.
"I don't think we have arrived at a turning point in the trend, but it was a significant correction," Gazdik said.
